note: Single source for command boundaries. Rendered into OpenCode permission rules. Edit this file, then run scripts/render.ps1.

rules.why: These rewrite or wipe local history. Inspect and make a focused reversible change instead.
These throw away uncommitted work with no undo. Inspect and revert exact files instead.
Deleting a remote release or cache is never an incidental development action. Do it by hand after verifying the exact target.
A commit is the user's record of the work. Draft the message. Do not run git commit.
Opening, merging, and closing work on GitHub is visible to other people the moment it runs, and approval for one does not carry to the next.
Reading a credential into the transcript exposes it to the model provider and to anyone the transcript is later shared with.
rules.why_read_paths: A file-read boundary, not a command boundary, which is why the commands array is empty. OpenCode renders these as permission.read entries. The Hermes hook matches them before a read.
